cues.en: Most of the time I do not read my talks. I plan the main points and then speak off the top of my head. But for this talk, I need to stick to a text and for good cause. Please bear with me. I think you know what a man is. A woman is more or less like a man, but not of the same sex. This may seem like a strange thing for me to start with, but soon you will see why. Next, I shall say that a person is a woman or a man, young or old. And to keep things short,
cues.zh: 多数时候我不读稿。我只规划要点，然后即兴讲。但这次演讲我得照着文字讲，而且有充分理由。请多包涵。我想你知道男人是什么。女人大体像男人，但性别不同。我这样开头可能有点怪，但很快你会明白为什么。接下来我要说，一个人要么是女人，要么是男人，无论年轻或年老。简而言之，

cues.en: When I say he, I mean he or she, and when I say his, I mean his or her. A machine is a thing that can do a task with no help or not much help from a person. As a rule, we can speak of two or more of a thing if we add an S or Z sound to the end of a word that names it. These are names of persons. Alan Turing, Alonzo Church, Charles K. Ogden, Christopher Alexander, Eric Raymond, Fred Brooks,
cues.zh: 我说“他”时，指他或她；我说“他的”时，指他的或她的。机器是能在没有或很少人帮助下完成任务的东西。通常，在命名某物的词末尾加一个 S 或 Z 音，就可以指两个或更多该事物。这些是人名。Alan Turing、Alonzo Church、Charles K. Ogden、Christopher Alexander、Eric Raymond、Fred Brooks，

cues.en: John Horton Conway, James Gosling, Bill Joy, and Dick Gabriel. The word other means not the same. The phrase other than means not the same as. A number may be not, or maybe one more than a number. In this way, we have a set of numbers with no bound. There are other numbers as well, but I shall not speak more of them yet. These numbers, not, or one more than a number, can be used to count things. We can add two numbers,
cues.zh: John Horton Conway、James Gosling、Bill Joy 和 Dick Gabriel。other 这个词意为不相同。other than 这个短语意为与……不相同。一个数可以是零，或者比某个数多一。这样我们就得到一组没有上界的数。还有其他数，但我先不多讲。这些数——零，或比某个数多一——可用来计数。我们可以把两个数相加，

cues.en: If we count up from the first number, while we count down from the number that is not the first till it come to naught, then the first count is the sum. We shall take the word many to mean more than two, more than two in number. Now, think of a machine that can keep track of two numbers and count each one up or down, and test if a number be naught, and by such a test, choose to do this or that. The list of things it can do, and the choices that it can make,
cues.zh: 如果从第一个数往上数，同时从不是第一个的那个数往下数，直到它变成零，那么第一个计数就是和。我们把 many 一词理解为多于两个，也就是数量多于二。现在设想一台机器，它能记录两个数，能把每个数加一或减一，能测试某个数是否为零，并根据这种测试选择做这件事或那件事。它能做的事情清单，以及它能做的选择，

cues.en: must be of a known size that is some number. Here, you can see two numbers and a list. Each row in the list has a state name, the word up or down, and which number to count up or count down. For up, we have the name of the next state to go to, and the machine counts the number up by one. For down, the machine first tests the number, and so we have the name of the new state to go to if the number be not.
cues.zh: 必须具有已知大小，也就是某个数。这里你能看到两个数和一个列表。列表的每一行有一个状态名、单词 up 或 down，以及要对哪个数加一或减一。对 up，我们有下一个要转到的状态名，机器把该数加一。对 down，机器先测试该数，因此我们有如果该数为零时要转到的新状态名。

cues.en: and the name of the new state to go to if the number be other than not, in which case the machine counts the number down by one. A computer is a machine that can do at least what that machine can. And we have good cause to think that if a computer task can be done at all, then the two number machine can do it too, if you put numbers in and read them out in the right way. In some sense, all computers are the same. We know this thanks to the work of such persons as Alan Turing and Alonzo Church. A vocabulary is a set of words.
cues.zh: 以及如果该数不为零时要转到的新状态名；这种情况下，机器把该数减一。计算机是一台至少能做那台机器所能做之事的机器。我们有充分理由认为，如果一项计算机任务能够完成，那么那台双数机器也能完成它——只要以正确的方式输入和读出数字。某种意义上，所有计算机都一样。我们之所以知道这一点，要感谢 Alan Turing 和 Alonzo Church 等人的工作。词汇是一组词。

cues.en: A language is a vocabulary and rules for what a string of words might mean to a person or a machine that hears them. To define a word is to tell what it means. When you define a word, you add it to your vocabulary and to the vocabulary of each person who hears you. Then you can use the word. To program is to make up a list of things to do and choices to make, to be done by a computer. Such a list is called a program.
cues.zh: 语言是一套词汇和规则，用来确定一串词对听到它的人或机器可能意味着什么。定义一个词，就是说明它是什么意思。当你定义一个词时，你把它加入自己的词汇表，也加入每个听你说话的人的词汇表。然后你就能用这个词了。编程就是列出一份要做的事情和要做的选择，交给计算机去执行。这样一份清单叫作程序。

cues.en: Next, a noun can be made from a verb to mean that which is done as meant by the verb. To make such a noun, we add ing to the verb stem. Thus, we can speak of programming. A programming language is a language that we can use to tell a computer a program to do. Java is a brand name for a computer programming language. I shall speak of the Java programming language a great deal more in this talk. I have to say the full phrase, the Java programming language,
cues.zh: 接下来，名词可以由动词构成，表示按该动词所表达的意思而被完成的事情。要构成这样的名词，我们在动词词干后加 ing。于是，我们就可以说 programming（编程）。编程语言是一种语言，我们能用它告诉计算机要执行的程序。Java 是一种计算机编程语言的商标名。在这次演讲中，我还会大量谈到 Java 编程语言。我必须说完整的说法，Java 编程语言，

cues.en: For there is a guy who works where I do who deals with the laws of marks of trade, and he told me I have to say it that way. Names of other programming languages are Fortran, APL, Pascal, and PL1. A part of a program that defines a new word for use in other parts of the program is called a definition. Not all programming languages have a way to code definitions, but most do. Those that do not are for wimps. Should a programming language be large or small? A small programming language might take but a short time to learn.
cues.zh: 因为在我工作的地方，有个人负责商标法，他告诉我必须那样说。其他编程语言的名字有 Fortran、APL、Pascal 和 PL1。程序中定义新词、供程序其他部分使用的那部分，叫作定义。并非所有编程语言都有办法编写定义，但大多数都有。没有的，是给弱者用的。编程语言应该大还是小？一门小的编程语言可能只需要很短时间就能学会。

cues.en: A large programming language may take a long, long time to learn, but then it is less hard to use. For then we have a lot of words at hand, or I should say, at the tips of our tongues, to use at the drop of a hat. If we start with a small language, then in most cases we cannot say much at the start. We must first define more words. Then we can speak of the main thing that is on our mind. We can use a verb in the past tense if we add a duh or ed sound at the end of the verb. In the same way, we can form what we call a past participle.
cues.zh: 一门大的编程语言可能要花很久很久才能学会，但之后就比较不那么难用。因为那时我们手边有很多词——或者我该说，舌尖上有很多词——可以随时拿来用。如果我们从一门小语言开始，那么在大多数情况下，一开始说不了多少东西。我们必须先定义更多词。然后才能说出心里想的主要事情。如果在动词末尾加一个 duh 或 ed 的音，我们就能用过去时。用同样的方式，我们可以构成所谓的过去分词。

cues.en: which is a form of the verb that says of a noun that what the verb means has been done to it. For this talk, I wanted to show you what it is like to use a language that is much too small. You've now had a good taste of it. I must next define a few more words. An example is some one thing out of a set of things that I put in front of you so that you can see how some part of that thing is in fact a part of each thing in the set. A syllable is a bit of sound that a mouth and a tongue can say all at one time.
cues.zh: 它是动词的一种形式，用来说明某个名词已经承受了该动词所表示的动作。在这次演讲中，我想让你们体会一下使用一门过于小的语言是什么感觉。你们现在已经尝到不少滋味了。接下来我必须再定义几个词。例子，就是我从摆在你面前的一组事物中挑出的某一个事物，好让你看到这个事物的某个部分其实也是这组中每个事物的一部分。音节是嘴和舌头能一次连续发出的那一小段声音。

cues.en: more or less, in a smooth way. Each word is made up of one or more syllables. A primitive is a word for which we can take it for granted that we all know what it means. For this talk, I chose to take as my primitives all the words of one syllable and no more, from the language I use for most of my speech each day, which is called English. My firm rule for this talk is that if I need to use a word of two or more syllables, I must first define it. Thank you. Now you see.
cues.zh: 大致上，是以一种流畅的方式。每个词由一个或多个音节组成。基本词是我们理所当然地认为大家都知道其含义的词。为了这次演讲，我选择把日常大部分讲话所用语言中所有只有一个音节、不多于一个音节的词，作为我的基本词；这门语言叫英语。我这次演讲的硬性规则是：如果我需要用两个或更多音节的词，我必须先定义它。谢谢。现在你们明白了。

cues.en: I can do this by defining one word at a time, and I have done so, or I can give a rule by which a new word can be made from some other known word, so that many new words can be defined at once, and I have done this as well. This choice, to start with just words of one syllable, was why I had to define the word woman, but could take the word man for granted. I wanted to define the word machine in terms of the word person, and it seemed least hard to define person as a man or a woman.
cues.zh: 我可以一次只定义一个词，我也确实这么做了；或者我也可以给出一个规则，用已知的词来构造新词，从而一次性定义许多新词，我也同样这么做了。之所以选择只从单音节词开始，是因为我不得不定义“woman”这个词，而“man”则可以直接使用。我想用“person”来定义“machine”，而把“person”定义为一个“man”或一个“woman”似乎最简单。

cues.en: But then, by chance, the word man has one syllable, and so is a primitive in English. But the word woman has two syllables, and so I had to define it. In a language other than English, the words that mean man and woman might each have one syllable, or might each have two syllables, in which case one would have to take some other tack. We have to do this a lot when we write real computer programs. A thought that seems like a primitive in our minds turns out not to be a primitive in a programming language. And in each new program, we must define it once more.
cues.zh: 但碰巧的是，“man”是单音节词，因此在英语里是个原语。但“woman”有两个音节，所以我必须先定义它。在英语以外的语言里，表示男人和女人的词可能都是单音节，也可能都是双音节，那样的话就得另寻他法了。我们在编写实际的计算机程序时经常要做这种事。一个在我们脑海中看似原语的想法，在编程语言中却并不是原语。而在每一个新程序中，我们都必须重新定义它一次。

cues.en: A good example of this is MAX, which yields the more large of two numbers. It is a primitive thought to me, but few programming languages have it as a primitive. I have to define it. This is the sort of thing that makes a computer look like a person who is but four years old. Next to English, all computer programming languages are small. As we write code, we must stop now and then to define some new term that we will need to use in more than one place. Some persons find that their programs have a few large chunks of code that do the real work.
cues.zh: MAX 就是个很好的例子，它返回两个数中较大的那个。对我来说它是一个原生想法，但很少有编程语言把它作为原语。我必须自己定义它。正是这种事情，让计算机看起来像个只有四岁的小孩。相比英语，所有的计算机编程语言都很简小。在我们写代码时，必须时不时停下来去定义一些需要在多处使用的新术语。有些人发现他们的程序包含几大块负责核心工作的代码，

cues.en: plus a large pile of small bits of code that define new words, so to speak, to be used as if they were primitives. I hope that this talk brings home to you in a way that you can feel in your heart, not just think in your head, what it is like to have to program in that way. This should show you true to life what it is like to use a small language. Each time I have tried this sort of thing, I have found that I cannot say much at all until I take the time to define at least a few new terms. In other words,
cues.zh: 外加一大堆细碎的代码，可以说是用来定义各种“新词”，好让我们像使用原语一样使用它们。我希望这场演讲能让你切身感受到——而不仅仅是用头脑去想——以这种方式编程到底是什么体验。这应该能让你逼真地体会到使用一门微小语言是什么感觉。每次我尝试这样做，都会发现如果不花时间先定义至少几个新术语，我根本就说不了什么话。换句话说，

cues.en: If you want to get far at all with a small language, you must first add to the small language to make a language that is more large. In some cases, we will find it more smooth to add the syllable er to the end of a word, then to use the word more in front of it. In this way, we might say smoother in place of more smooth. Let me add that better means more good. In truth, the words one syllable form quite a rich vocabulary with which you can say many things.
cues.zh: 如果你想用一门微小语言走得更远，就必须先扩充它，让它变得更庞大。在某些情况下，我们会发现在词尾加上音节 -er，比在前面加 more 更顺畅。这样一来，我们就可以用 smoother 来代替 more smooth。我顺便补充一句，better 的意思就是 more good。实际上，单音节词构成了一个相当丰富的词汇库，足以用来表达很多事情。

cues.en: You may note that this vocabulary is much larger than that of a language called Basic English, defined by Charles K. Ogden in the year 193-0. I chose not to use Basic English this talk, the cause being that Basic English has many words with two or more syllables, some of them quite long, handed down to us from the dim past of Rome. While Basic English has fewer words, it does not give the feel to one who speaks full English of being a small language.
cues.zh: 大家可能会注意到，这里的词汇量远大于 Charles K. Ogden 在1930年定义的一种名为 Basic English 的语言。我之所以在本次演讲中选择不用 Basic English，是因为它包含许多双音节或多音节词，其中一些相当长，是从古罗马遥远的过去流传下来的。虽然 Basic English 的词汇量较少，但对说完整英语的人来说，它给人的感觉并不像一门精简小巧的语言。

cues.en: By the way, from now on, I shall use the word because to mean the cause being that. If we look at English and then at programming languages, we see that all our programming languages seem small. And yet we can say too, in some cases, that one programming language is smaller than some other programming language. A design is a plan for how to build a thing. To design is to build a thing in one's mind, but not yet in the real world. Or better yet, to plan how the real thing can be built. The main thing that I want to ask in this talk is,
cues.zh: 顺便说一句，从现在开始，我将用 because 这个词来表示“原因在于”。如果我们看看英语，再看看编程语言，就会发现我们所有的编程语言看起来都很小。然而在某些情况下，我们也可以说，某门编程语言比另一门更小。设计，就是对如何构建某物的规划。设计是在脑海中构建某物，而非在现实世界中构建。或者更确切地说，是规划如何在现实中构建它。我在本次演讲中主要想探讨的是：

cues.en: If I want to help other persons to write all sorts of programs, should I design a small programming language or a large one? I stand on this claim. I should not design a small language, and I should not design a large one. I need to design a language that can grow. I need to plan ways in which it might grow, but I need to to leave some choices so that other persons can make those choices at a later time. This is not a new thought. We have known for some time that huge programs cannot be coded from scratch all at once.
cues.zh: 如果我想帮助其他人编写各种程序，我是应该设计一门小型编程语言，还是一门大型编程语言？我坚持这样一个观点：我不应该设计小型语言，也不应该设计大型语言。我需要设计一门能够演进增长的语言。我需要规划它可能的增长方式，但也需要留出一些选择空间，以便其他人在以后做出决断。这并不是什么新想法。我们早就知道，庞大的程序不可能一蹴而就地从零编写出来。

cues.en: There has to be a plan for growth. What we must stop to think on now is the fact that languages have now reached that large size where they cannot be designed all at once, much less built all at once. Let me pause to define some names for numbers. 20 is twice 10. 30 is thrice 10. 40 is twice 20. 100 is 10 times 10. A million is 100 times 100 times 100. 16 is twice 8. 7 is 1 plus 6.
cues.zh: 必须要有演进增长的规划。我们现在必须停下来反思的是：编程语言如今已庞大到无法一次性设计完成，更不用说一次性构建完成了。请允许我暂停一下，给几个数字下个定义：20是10的两倍；30是10的三倍；40是20的两倍；100是10乘10；一百万是100乘100再乘100；16是8的两倍；7是1加6。

cues.en: 50 is one more than seven squared. One more thing. A go means in the past, counting back from now. In the past, it made sense to design a whole language once for all. Fortran was a small language 40 years ago, designed for tasks with numbers, and it served well. PL1 was thought a big language 30 years ago, but now we would think of it as small. Pascal was designed as a small whole language with no plan to add to it later. That was five and 20 years ago.
cues.zh: 50比7的平方多1。还有一件事：ago 的意思是从现在往前数的过去时间。在过去，一劳永逸地设计一门完整的语言是有道理的。40年前，Fortran 是一门小语言，专为数值任务设计，而且表现出色。30年前，PL1 被认为是一门大语言，但现在看来它其实很小。Pascal 当初被设计成一门完整的小型语言，并没有后续扩充的计划。那是25年前的事了。

cues.en: What came to pass? Fortran has grown and grown. Many new words and many new rules have been added. The new design is not bad. The parts fit well, one with the other. But to many programmers who have used Fortran for a long time, the Fortran of here and now is not at all the same as the language they first came to know and love. It looks strange. PL1 has not grown much. It is for the most part, just as it was when it first came out. It may be that this is from lack of use.
cues.zh: 后来发生了什么呢？Fortran 不断演进壮大，增加了许多新词汇和许多新规则。新的设计并不差，各部分之间契合得很好。但对许多长期使用 Fortran 的程序员来说，如今的 Fortran 已经完全不同于他们最初熟悉并喜爱的那个语言了，它看起来很陌生。而 PL1 则没有太大增长，在很大程度上依然是刚问世时的样子。这可能是因为用的人太少了。

cues.en: The flip side is that the lack of use may have two causes. Number one, PO1 was not designed to grow. It was designed to be all things to all programmers right from the start. Number two, for its time, it started out large. No one knew all of PO1. Some said that no one could know all of PO1. Pascal grew just a tad and was used to build many large programs. One main fault of the first design was that strings were hard to use because they were all a fixed size.
cues.zh: 另一面是，使用不足可能有两个原因。第一，PO1 并不是为增长而设计的。它从一开始就设计成对所有程序员都面面俱到。第二，在它那个年代，它起步时就很大。没人了解整个 PO1。有人说没人能了解整个 PO1。Pascal 只增长了一点点，就被用来构建许多大型程序。最初设计的一个主要缺陷是字符串难用，因为它们全是固定长度。

cues.en: Pascal would have been of no use for the building of large programs for use in the real world if this had not been changed. But Wirth had not planned for the language to change in such ways, and in fact, few changes were made. At times, we think of C as a small language designed from whole cloth. But it grew out of a smaller language called B, and has since grown to be a larger language called C++. A language as large as C++ could not have spread so wide if it had been foisted on the world all at once. It would have been too hard to port. One more rule for making words.
cues.zh: 如果不改变这一点，Pascal 对构建现实世界的大型程序就毫无用处。但 Wirth 并没有计划让语言以这种方式变化，事实上改动也很少。有时我们会把 C 看作一门凭空设计出来的小语言。但它其实是从一门更小的语言 B 发展而来，后来又长成了更大的 C++。像 C++ 这么大的语言，如果一次性强推给全世界，不可能传播得这么广。那会太难移植。造词的又一条规则。

cues.en: If we add the syllable er to a verb stem, we make a noun that names the person or thing that does what the verb says to do. For example, a buyer is one who buys. A user is one who uses. As you may by now have guessed, I am of like mind with my good friend Dick Gabriel, here in the front row, who wrote the well-known screed, Worse is Better. The real name was lisp. Good news, bad news, how to win big. Which is all words of just one syllable.
cues.zh: 如果把音节 er 加到动词词干上，我们就造出一个名词，表示做该动词所说之事的人或物。例如，buyer 就是买东西的人。user 就是使用的人。你可能已经猜到了，我和前排的好友 Dick Gabriel 想法一致，他写了那篇著名的文章《Worse is Better》。真名是 Lisp。好消息、坏消息、如何大获全胜。这些词都只有一个音节。

cues.en: which might seem like good luck for me, but the truth is that Dick Gabriel knew how to choose words with punch. Yet what first comes to mind for most persons is the part-headed, worse is better, and so that's how they cite it. The gist of it is that the best way to get a language used by many persons is not to design and build the right thing, because that will take too long. In a race, a small language with warts will beat a well-designed language because users will not wait for the right thing. They will use the language that is quick and cheap and put up with the warts.
cues.zh: 这对我来说似乎算好运，但事实是 Dick Gabriel 懂得如何挑选有冲击力的词。然而大多数人首先想到的是那句硬邦邦的“Worse is Better”，所以他们就这么引用。其要点是，让一门语言被很多人使用的最好办法，不是设计并构建出正确的东西，因为那会花太久。在竞赛中，一门有瑕疵的小语言会击败设计良好的语言，因为用户不会等正确的东西。他们会用快速、便宜的语言，并容忍瑕疵。

cues.en: Once a small language fills a niche, it is hard to take its place. Well then, could not the right thing be a small language, not hard to part port, but with no warts? I guess it could be done, but I, for one, am not that smart, or have not had that much luck. But in fact, I think it cannot be done. Five and 20 years ago, when users did not want that much from a language, one could try. Scheme was my best shot at it.
cues.zh: 一旦一门小语言占据了一个生态位，就很难取代它。那么，“正确的东西”难道不能是一门小语言吗？不难移植，而且没有瑕疵？我想这也许能做到，但就我而言，我没那么聪明，或者运气没那么好。但事实上，我认为这做不到。25 年前，用户对语言的要求还没那么高，还可以试一试。Scheme 是我对此最好的尝试。

cues.en: But users will not now, with glad cries, glom onto a language that gives them no more than what schema Pascal gave them. They need to paint bits, lines, and boxes on the screen in hues bright and wild. They need to talk to printers and servers through the net. They need to load code on the fly. They need their programs to work with other code they don't trust. They need to run code in many threads and on many machines. They need to deal with text and sayings in all the world's languages. A small programming language just won't cut it.
cues.zh: 但现在的用户不会欢呼着追捧一门只给他们 Scheme 和 Pascal 那些东西的语言。他们需要在屏幕上用明亮狂野的色彩绘制位、线和方框。他们需要通过网络与打印机和服务器通信。他们需要动态加载代码。他们需要让自己的程序与他们不信任的其他代码协作。他们需要在许多线程和许多机器上运行代码。他们需要处理全世界各种语言的文本和语句。一门小语言根本不够用。

cues.en: So a small language cannot do the job right, and a large language takes too long to get off the ground. Are we doomed to use small languages with many warts because that is the sole kind of design that can make it in the world? At one time, this thought filled me with gloom. But then I saw a gap in my thinking. I said that users will not wait for the right thing, but will use what comes first and put up with the warts. But users will not put up with the warts for all time.
cues.zh: 小语言做不好这件事，大语言又要花太久才能起步。那我们是不是注定要用满是毛病的小语言，因为只有这种设计才能流行起来？有一段时间，这个想法让我很沮丧。但后来我发现自己的思路里有个漏洞。我说过，用户不会等那个正确的东西，而是先用先出现的东西，并忍受毛病。但用户不会永远忍受毛病。

cues.en: It is not long till they scream and moan and beg for changes. The small language will grow. The warts will be shaved off or patched. If one person does all the work, then growth will be slow. But if one lets the users help do the work, growth can be quick. If many persons work side by side and the best work is added with care and good taste, a great deal can be added in a short time. APL was designed by one man, a smart man, and I love APL.
cues.zh: 用不了多久，他们就会抱怨、哀嚎，求着要改。小语言会成长。毛病会被削掉或打上补丁。如果所有工作都由一个人做，成长就会很慢。但如果让用户帮忙做，成长就能很快。如果许多人并肩工作，再把最好的成果用心、有品味地加进来，短时间内就能加进很多东西。APL 由一个人设计，一个聪明人，而我很喜欢 APL。

cues.en: But it had a flaw that I think has all but killed it. There was no way for a user to grow the language in a smooth way. In most languages, a user can at least define some new words to stand for other pieces of code that can then be called in such a way that the new words look like primitives. In this way, a user can build a larger language to meet his needs. But in APL, new words defined by the user do not look like language primitives at all. The name of a piece of user code is a word.
cues.zh: 但它有一个缺陷，我认为几乎害死了它。用户没办法平滑地扩展这门语言。在大多数语言里，用户至少可以定义一些新词来代表其他代码片段，然后以让新词看起来像原语的方式调用它们。这样，用户就能构建更大的语言来满足需求。但在 APL 里，用户定义的新词完全不像语言原语。一段用户代码的名字就是一个词。

cues.en: But things that are built in are named by strange glyphs. To add what look like new primitives, to keep the feel of the language, takes a real hacker and a ton of work. This has stopped users from helping to grow the language. APL has grown some, but the work has been done by just the few programmers that have the source code. If a user adds to APL, and what he added seems like a good idea to the hackers in charge of the language, they might then make it be built in. But the code to use it would not look the same.
cues.zh: 但内置的东西却用奇怪的符号命名。要添加看起来像新原语的东西，还要保持语言的感觉，需要真正的黑客和大量工作。这阻止了用户帮忙扩展语言。APL 确实有所成长，但工作只由少数拥有源码的程序员完成。如果用户给 APL 添加了东西，而负责这门语言的黑客们觉得是个好主意，他们可能会把它内置。但使用它的代码看起来会不一样。

cues.en: The user would have to change his code to a new form, because an APL, a use of what is built in, does not look at all like a quality user code. Lisp was designed by one man, a smart man, and it works in a way that I think he did not plan for. In Lisp, new words defined by the user look like primitives, and what is more, all primitives look like words defined by the user. In other words, if a user has good taste in defining new words, what comes out is a larger language that has no seams.
cues.zh: 用户将不得不把自己的代码改成新形式，因为 APL 里对内置功能的使用，看起来完全不像优质的用户代码。Lisp 由一个人设计，一个聪明人，而它的运作方式我认为他并没有计划过。在 Lisp 里，用户定义的新词看起来像原语，而且所有原语看起来也像用户定义的新词。换句话说，如果用户在定义新词时有品味，得到的就是一门无缝的更大语言。

cues.en: The designer in charge can grow the language with close to no work on his part just by choosing with care from the work of many users. And Lisp grew much faster than APL did, because many users could try things out and put their best code out there for others to use and to add to the language. Lisp is not used quite as much as it used to be, but parts of it live on in other languages, the best of which is called garbage collection. And I will not try to tell you now what that means in words of one syllable.
cues.zh: 负责人几乎不用自己动手，只要从众多用户的工作中精心挑选，就能扩展语言。而且 Lisp 的成长比 APL 快得多，因为许多用户都能尝试，并把自己最好的代码放出来，供别人使用并加入语言。Lisp 现在用得没以前那么多了，但它的一部分在其他语言中延续下来，其中最棒的是垃圾回收。我现在不打算用大白话解释那是什么意思。

cues.en: I leave it to you as a task to try in your spare time. It is not that hard. This leads me to claim that from now on, a main goal in designing a language should be to plan for growth. The language must start small, and the language must grow as the set of users grows. I now think that I, as a language designer helping out with the Java programming language, need to ask not, should the Java programming language grow, but how should the Java programming language grow? There is more than one kind of growth.
cues.zh: 我把这个留给你们当个小作业，闲暇时可以试试。这并不难。这让我得出这样一个结论：从现在起，设计一门语言的主要目标，应当是为成长做好规划。语言必须从小起步，而且必须随着用户群体的壮大而成长。我现在认为，我作为协助开发 Java 编程语言的语言设计者，需要问的不是 Java 编程语言是否应该成长，而是它应该如何成长？成长的方式不止一种，

cues.en: and more than one way to do it. But as we shall see, if the goal is to be quick and yet to do good work, one mode may be better by far than all others. There are two kinds of growth in a language. One can change the vocabulary, or one can change the rules that say what a string of words means. A library is a vocabulary designed to be added to a programming language to make its vocabulary larger. A true library does not change the rules of meaning for the language, it just adds new words. You can see from this
cues.zh: 实现它的途径也不止一条。但正如我们将看到的，如果目标是既快又好，那么有一种模式远胜其他所有模式。一门语言有两种成长方式。你可以改变词汇，或者改变决定一串词含义的规则。库就是设计用来加入编程语言中、以扩充其词汇量的词汇表。真正的库不会改变语言的语义规则，它只是添加新词。由此可见，

cues.en: that in my view, the code that lets you do a long jump in C is not a true library. Of course, there must be a way for a user to make libraries, but the key point is that the new words defined by a library should look just like the primitives of the language. Some languages are like this and some are not. Those that are not are harder to grow with the help of users. It may be good as well to have a way to add to the rules of meaning for a language. Some ways to do this work better than others. But in the same way,
cues.zh: 在我看来，在 C 语言中让你实现长跳转的代码并不是真正的库。当然，必须有一种让用户能够构建库的方法，但关键在于，由库定义的新词看起来应该和语言原本的原语完全一样。有些语言是这样的，有些则不是。那些不是这样的语言，就更难借助用户的力量去成长。如果有办法扩展语言的语义规则，那可能也不错。有些做法比其他的更有效。但同样的，

cues.en: The language should let work done by a user look just like what was designed at the start. I would like to grow the Java brand programming language in such a way that users can do more of this. In the same way, there are two ways to do the growing. One is for one person or a small group to be in charge and to take in, test, judge, and add the work done by others. The other way is to just put the source code out there once things start to work and let each person do as he wills.
cues.zh: 语言应该让用户做出的东西，看起来和最初内置的设计别无二致。我希望以这样一种方式来发展 Java 编程语言，让用户能更多地做到这一点。同样地，推动成长也有两种方式。一种是由一个人或一个小团队负责，负责接收、测试、评审并合入其他人完成的工作。另一种方式是一旦代码能跑了，就把源代码直接公开，任由大家各随己愿。

cues.en: To have a person in charge can slow things down, but to have no one in charge makes it harder to add up the work of many persons. The way that I think is faster and better than all others does both. Put the source code out there and let all persons play with it, but have a person in charge who is a quick judge of good work and who will take it in and shove it back out fast. You don't have to use what he ships and you don't have to give back your work, but he gives all persons a fast way to spread new code to those who want it. The best example of this way to do things
cues.zh: 有人负责可能会拖慢进度，但如果无人负责，又很难把众人的工作整合在一起。我认为有一种比其他所有方式都更快更好的途径，它把两者结合了起来。把源代码公开，让大家都能上手玩，但同时保留一个负责人，他能迅速甄别优秀的成果，并快速吸收进来、再推发出去。你并不一定要用他发布的东西，也未必要回馈你的工作，但他为大家提供了一种快速途径，把新代码分发给想要它的人。这种方式最好的范例

cues.en: is Linux, which is an operating system, which is a program that keeps track of other programs in a computer and gives each its due in time and space. Do you like that? You ought to read what Eric Raymond had to say of how Linux came to be. I shall tell you a bit of it once I define two more words for you. A cathedral is a huge church. It may be made of stone. It may fill you with awe. But the key thought in the mind of Eric Raymond is that there is but one design.
cues.zh: 就是 Linux。Linux 是一个操作系统，也就是一个在计算机中跟踪其他程序、并在时间和空间上给予各程序应得资源的程序。你们喜欢这个定义吗？你们应该去读读 Eric Raymond 关于 Linux 是如何诞生的论述。等我再为你们定义两个词，我就讲讲这其中的故事。大教堂是一座巨大的教堂。它可能是石头砌成的。它可能会让你肃然起敬。但在 Eric Raymond 心中，核心思想在于它只有一个统一的设计。

cues.en: one grand plan, which may take a long time, many years to make real. As the years pass, few changes are made to the plan. Many, many persons are needed to build it, but there is just one designer. A bazaar is a place with many small shops or stalls where you can buy things from many persons who are there to sell their wares. The key thought here is that each one sells what he wants to sell and each one buys what he wants to buy. There is no one plan and each seller or buyer may change his mind at any time.
cues.zh: 一个宏伟计划，可能需要很长时间、很多年才能真正实现。随着岁月流逝，这个计划很少被改动。建造它需要许许多多人，但设计师只有一个。集市是一个有许多小店铺或摊位的地方，你可以在那里从许多前来售卖货物的人手中买东西。这里的关键思想是，每个人都卖自己想卖的东西，每个人都买自己想买的东西。这里没有统一计划，每个卖家或买家都可以随时改变主意。

cues.en: Eric Raymond wrote a short work called The Cathedral and the Bazaar, in which he looks at how programs are built or have been built in the past. You can find it on his website. He talks of how he built a mail fetching program with the help of more than 200 users. He quotes Fred Brooks as saying, more users find more bugs, and backs him up with tales from this example of building a program in the bizarre style. As for the role of programmer in charge,
cues.zh: Eric Raymond 写了一篇短文《大教堂与集市》，探讨了程序如今如何构建、以及过去曾如何构建。你可以在他的网站上找到它。他谈到自己如何在 200 多名用户的帮助下构建了一个邮件抓取程序。他引用 Fred Brooks 的话说，用户越多，发现的 bug 越多，并用这个以奇特风格构建程序的例子中的故事来佐证。至于负责程序员的作用，

cues.en: Eric Raymond says that it is fine to come up with good thoughts, but much better to know them when you see them in the works of others. You can get a lot more done that way. Linux rose to its heights of fame and wide use in much the same way, though on a much larger scale. To take this thought to the far end of the line, it may be that one could write an operating system by putting a million apes to work at a million typing machines, then just spotting the bits of good work that come out by chance and pasting them up to make a hole.
cues.zh: Eric Raymond 说过，自己能想到好点子固然不错，但能在别人的成果中一眼认出好点子则要好得多。这样你可以做成更多事情。Linux 能声名大噪并得到广泛应用，走的也大致是这条路，只不过规模要宏大得多。如果把这个思路推向极致，也许让一百万只猴子坐在一百万台打字机前，我们只要挑出它们碰巧敲出的优秀片段，再拼凑在一起，就能写出一个完整的操作系统了。

cues.en: But that might take a long time, I guess. Too bad. But the key point of the bazaar is not that you can get many persons to work with you at a task. For cathedral builders, had a great deal of help, too. Nor is the key point that you get help with the designing as well as the building, though that is, in fact, a big win. No, the key point is that in the bazaar style of building a program or designing a language, or what you will, the plan can change in real time to meet the needs of those who are working on it.
cues.zh: 但那大概要花很长时间，我猜。太糟了。不过，集市的关键点并不是你能让很多人和你一起做一项任务。教堂建造者也得到过大量帮助。关键点也不是你既能得到设计上的帮助，也能得到建造上的帮助，尽管这实际上是个巨大的优势。不，关键在于，用集市风格构建程序、设计语言，或者随便做什么时，计划可以实时改变，以满足正在参与其中的人的需求。

cues.en: This tends to make users stay with it as time goes by. They will take joy in working hard and helping out if they know that their wants and needs have some weight and their hard work can change the plan for the better, their better. Which brings me to the high point of my talk. It seems, in the last few years at least, that if one is asked to speak at this meeting, one must quote Christopher Alexander.
cues.zh: 随着时间推移，这往往会让用户留下来。如果用户知道自己的愿望和需求有一定分量，自己的努力能让计划变得更好——让他们自己更好，他们就会乐于努力付出、帮忙。这就带到了我演讲的高潮。至少在过去几年里，似乎只要被邀请在这个会议上发言，就一定要引用 Christopher Alexander。

cues.en: I know a bit of his work, though not a lot, and I must say thanks to Dick Gabriel for pointing out to me a quote that has a lot to do with the main point of this talk. I am sad to say that I do not know what this quote means, because Christopher Alexander uses many words of more than one syllable, and does not define them first. But I have learned to say these words by rote, and it may be that you out there can glean some thoughts of use to you. Christopher Alexander says, master plans have two additional unhealthy
cues.zh: 我了解他的一些工作，虽然不算多。我得感谢 Dick Gabriel 向我指出了一句引文，它和这次演讲的主旨有很大关系。很遗憾，我不知道这句引文是什么意思，因为 Christopher Alexander 用了很多不止一个音节的词，而且没有先定义它们。但我已经学会死记硬背地说这些词，也许你们在座的人能从中得到一些有用的想法。Christopher Alexander 说，总体规划还有两个额外的不健康……

cues.en: characteristics. To begin with, the existence of a master plan alienates the users. After all, the very existence of a master plan means, by definition, that the members of the community can have little impact on the future shape of their community, because most of the important decisions have already been made. In a sense, under a master plan, people are living with a frozen future, able to affect only relatively trivial details.
cues.zh:
特征。
首先，总体规划的存在会让用户产生疏离感。
毕竟，从定义上说，总体规划的存在就意味着社区成员几乎无法影响社区未来的形态，因为大多数重要决策早已作出。
某种意义上，在总体规划之下，人们面对的是一个被冻结的未来，只能影响相对无关紧要的细节。

cues.en: When people lose the sense of responsibility for the environment they live in, and realize they are merely cogs in someone else's machine, how can they feel any sense of identification with the community, or any sense of purpose there? I think this means, in part, that it is good to give your users a chance to buy in and pitch in. It is good for them, and it is good for you. In point of fact, a number of cathedrals were built in the bizarre mode.
cues.zh: 当人们对自己所处的环境失去责任感，并意识到自己只是别人机器上的齿轮时，他们怎么还能对社区有认同感，或在那里感到任何意义？我认为，这部分意味着，最好让你的用户有机会认同并参与进来。这对他们有好处，对你有好处。事实上，不少大教堂就是以这种奇怪的方式建成的。

cues.en: Does this mean, then, that it is of no use to design? Not at all. But instead of designing a thing, you need to design a way of doing. And this way of doing must make some choices now, but leave other choices to a later time. Which brings me to the word you have all been waiting for. A pattern is a plan that has some number of parts and shows you how each part turns a face to the others, how each joins with the others or stands off,
cues.zh: 那么，这是否意味着设计毫无用处？完全不是。但你需要设计的不是一件东西，而是一种做事方式。而这种做事方式必须现在做出一些选择，把另一些选择留到以后。这就引出了你们一直在等的那个词。模式是一种方案，它包含若干部分，并告诉你每个部分如何面向其他部分，如何与其他部分连接或保持独立，

cues.en: how each part does what it does and how the others aid it or drag it down, and how all the parts may be grasped as a whole and made to serve as one thing, for some higher goal or as part of a larger pattern. A pattern should give hints or clues as to when and where it is best put to use. What is more, some of the parts of a pattern may be holes or slots in which other things may be placed later. A good pattern will say how changes can be made in the course of time.
cues.zh: 每个部分如何完成自己的功能，其他部分如何帮助它或拖累它，以及所有部分如何作为一个整体被理解，并作为一个东西发挥作用，服务于更高目标，或作为更大模式的一部分。模式应提示或暗示何时何地最适合使用它。此外，模式的一些部分可以是空洞或槽位，之后可以在其中放入其他东西。好的模式会说明随时间推移可以如何修改。

cues.en: Thus, some choices of the plan are built in as part of the pattern, and other choices wait till the time when the pattern is to be used. In this way, a pattern stands for a design space in which you can choose on the fly your own path for growth and change. It is good to design a thing, but it can be far better and far harder to design a pattern. Best of all is to know when to use a pattern. Now for some more computer words. A datum is a set of bits.
cues.zh: 因此，方案中的一些选择作为模式的一部分内建，另一些选择则等到使用模式时才决定。这样，模式代表一个设计空间，你可以在其中即时选择自己的成长与变化路径。设计一个东西很好，但设计一个模式可能好得多，也难得多。最好的是知道何时使用模式。现在再说一些计算机术语。一个数据项是一组比特。

cues.en: Data is the mass noun for a set of datums. An object is a datum, the meanings of whose parts is laid down by a set of language rules. In the Java programming language, these rules use types to make clear which parts of an object may cite other objects. Objects may be grouped to form classes. Knowing the class of an object tells you most of what you need to know about how that object acts. Objects may have fields. Each field of an object can hold a datum. Which datum it holds may change from time to time.
cues.zh: Data 是表示一组数据项的不可数名词。对象就是一个数据项，其各部分的含义由一组语言规则规定。在 Java 编程语言中，这些规则用类型来明确对象的哪些部分可以引用其他对象。对象可以分组形成类。知道对象所属的类，就能了解该对象行为方式的大部分所需信息。对象可以有字段。对象的每个字段可以保存一个数据项。它保存哪个数据项可能不时变化。

cues.en: Each field may have a type which tells you what data can be in that field at runtime. And what is more, it tells you what data cannot be in that field at runtime. A method is a named piece of code that is part of an object. If you can name or cite an object, then you can call a method of that object. The method then does its thing. The Java programming language has objects and classes and fields and methods and types. Now I shall speak of some things that the Java programming language does not yet have.
cues.zh: 每个字段可以有一个类型，告诉你运行时该字段能放什么数据；更重要的是，它也告诉你运行时该字段不能放什么数据。方法是一段有名字的代码，是对象的一部分。如果你能命名或引用一个对象，就可以调用该对象的方法。然后方法执行它的功能。Java 编程语言有对象、类、字段、方法和类型。现在我要讲一些 Java 编程语言尚未具备的东西。

cues.en: A generic type is a map from one or more types to types. Put another way, a generic type is a pattern for building types. A number of groups of persons have set forth ways to add generic types to the Java programming language. Each way has its own good points. We heard three talks on adding generic types to the Java programming language at this meeting less than three and 20 hours ago. An operator is a glyph, such as a plus sign, that can be used in a language as if it were a word.
cues.zh: 泛型类型是从一个或多个类型到类型的映射。换句话说，泛型类型是构建类型的模板。已有不少团队提出了给 Java 编程语言添加泛型类型的方法。每种方法都各有千秋。就在不到 23 个小时前，我们还在本次会议上听了三场关于给 Java 添加泛型类型的演讲。运算符是一种字符符号，比如加号，在语言中用起来就像一个词一样。

cues.en: In the C or the Java programming language, as in English, the sign first known as and per se and is an operator. But a full stop or a quote mark is not an operator. A word is said to be overloaded if it is made to mean two or more things, and the hearer has to choose the meaning based on the rest of what is said. For example, using the rules defined near the start of this talk, a verb form such as painted might be a past tense or a past participle, and it is up to you, the hearer,
cues.zh: 在 C 或 Java 语言中，就像在英语中一样，最初被称为“&”的那个符号就是一个运算符。但句号或引号就不是运算符。如果一个词被赋予两种或更多含义，而且听者必须根据上下文来判断其意图，那么这个词就是“重载”的。例如，按照本次演讲开头定义的规则，像 painted 这样的动词形式可能是过去时，也可能是过去分词，这取决于作为听众的你，

cues.en: to make the call as to which I mean when I say it. Sometimes an overloaded word is called polymorphic, which means that the word has many forms. But the truth is that the word has but one form and many meanings. The definition of a word may be polymorphic, but the word as such is not. An operator can be overloaded in C++. But right now, operators in the Java programming language cannot be overloaded by the programmer, even though the names of methods may be overloaded. I would like to change that.
cues.zh: 在我说出它时去判断我指的是哪一种。有时，重载词也被称为多态的，意思是这个词有多种形态。但事实是，这个词只有一种形式，却有多种含义。词的定义或许是多态的，但词本身并不是。在 C++ 中，运算符是可以重载的。但目前在 Java 语言中，即使方法名可以重载，程序员也无法重载运算符。我想改变这一现状。

cues.en: I have said in the past, and will say now, that I think it would be a good thing for the Java programming language to add generic types and to let the user define overloaded operators. Just as a user can code methods that can be used in just the same way as methods that are built in, the user ought to have a way to define operators for user-defined classes that can be used in just the same way as operators that are built in. What is more, I would add a kind of class that is of lightweight, one whose objects can be cloned at will with no harm,
cues.zh: 我过去说过，现在也要重申，我认为给 Java 语言添加泛型类型并允许用户自定义重载运算符是一件好事。正如用户编写的方法使用起来与内置方法无异，用户也应该能够为自定义类定义运算符，并且用起来和内置运算符毫无差别。不仅如此，我还想添加一种轻量级的类，它的对象可以随意复制而没有任何危害，

cues.en: and so could be kept on a stack for speed, and not just in the heap. Classes of this kind would be well-suited for use as user-defined number types, but would have other uses too. You can find a plan for all this on a web page by James Gosling. There are a few other things we could add as well, such as tail calls, and ways to read and write those machine flags for numbers whose points float. But these are small language tweaks next to generic types in overloaded operators.
cues.zh: 从而可以保存在栈上以提升速度，而不仅仅是放在堆里。这种类非常适合用作自定义数值类型，但同样适用于其他场景。你可以在 James Gosling 的网页上找到关于这一切的规划。我们还可以添加其他一些特性，比如尾调用，以及读写浮点数机器标志位的方法。但与泛型类型和重载运算符相比，这些都只是语言上的小修小改。

cues.en: If we grow the language in these few ways, then I think we will not need to grow it in a hundred other ways. The users can take on the rest of the task. To see why, think on these examples. A complex number is a pair of numbers. There are rules for how to find the sum of two complex numbers. Are a complex number times a complex number? Some programmers like to use them a lot. Others do not use them at all. So, should we make complex number a type in the Java programming language?
cues.zh: 如果我们从这几个方面来扩展这门语言，我认为就不需要在其他上百个方面去扩展它了。剩下的任务用户完全可以自己搞定。想明白为什么，不妨思考这些例子。复数是一对数字。计算两个复数的和是有明确规则的。两个复数相乘也是如此。有些程序员非常频繁地使用它们。而另一些人则完全不用。那么，我们是否应该把复数做成 Java 语言内置的一种类型呢？

cues.en: Some say yes, of course. Many others say no. A rational number is a pair of numbers. There are rules, not the same as the rules for complex numbers, of course, for how to find the sum of two rational numbers, or a rational number times a rational number. A few programmers like to use them a lot. Most do not use them at all. So, should we make rational number a type in the Java programming language? An interval is a pair of numbers. There are rules, not the same as the rules for complex numbers or rational numbers, of course.
cues.zh: 当然，有人会说是，但也有很多人说不。有理数是一对数。当然，求两个有理数的和，或者有理数相乘，都有规则，且与复数的规则不同。少数程序员非常喜欢用它们，大多数人则根本不用。那么，我们是否应该把有理数作为 Java 编程语言的一种类型呢？区间也是一对数。当然也有规则，与复数或有理数的规则并不相同。

cues.en: for how to find the sum of two intervals or an interval times an interval. A few programmers like to use them a lot and wish all the other programmers who use numbers would use them too. But most do not use them at all. So should we make interval a type in the Java programming language? John Horton Conway once defined a game to be a pair of sets of games. See his book on numbers and games. Then he pointed out that some games may be thought of as numbers that say how many moves it will take to win the game.
cues.zh: 规定了如何求两个区间的和，或区间相乘。少数程序员非常喜欢用区间，并希望所有用数的程序员也都用上它们。但大多数人根本不用。那么，我们是否应该把区间作为 Java 编程语言的一种类型呢？John Horton Conway 曾把博弈定义为一对博弈集合，详见他关于数与博弈的书。然后他指出，有些博弈可以被看作是数，表示赢得比赛还需要走多少步。

cues.en: There are rules for how to find the sum of two games and so on. From this he worked out, for hundreds of kinds of real games, how to know which player will win. I think three persons in the world know how to use this kind of number. Should we make it a type in the Java programming language? A vector is a row of numbers all of the same type, with each place in the row named by the kind of number we first spoke of in this talk. There are rules.
cues.zh: 求两个博弈之和等操作也是有规则的。由此，他推导出了在数百种真实博弈中如何判断哪位玩家会获胜。我想全世界大概只有三个人知道怎么用这种数。我们应该把它做成 Java 编程语言的一种类型吗？向量是一排同类型的数，这一排中的每个位置都用我们开篇提到的那种数来命名。这里同样有规则。

cues.en: In fact, for vectors of length 3, there are two ways to do a vector times a vector, so you can have twice the fun. Vectors of length 3 or 4 are a great aid in making bits on the screen look like scenes in the real world. So should we make vector a type in the Java programming language? A matrix is a set of numbers laid out in a square, and there are rules. So should we make matrix a type in the Java programming language? And so on, and so on, and so on.
cues.zh: 事实上，对于长度为 3 的向量，向量相乘有两种方式，所以你能享受双倍的乐趣。长度为 3 或 4 的向量极大地帮助了把屏幕上的比特渲染成现实世界中的场景。那么我们应该把向量做成 Java 编程语言的一种类型吗？矩阵是排成方阵的一组数，也有其相应的规则。那么我们应该把矩阵做成 Java 编程语言的一种类型吗？以此类推，不胜枚举。

cues.en: I might say yes to each one of these, but it is clear that I must say no to all of them. And so would James Gosling and Bill Joy. To add them all to the Java programming language would be just too much. Some parts of the programming vocabulary are fit for all programmers to use, but other parts are just for their own niches. It would not be fair to weigh down all programmers with the need to have or to learn all the words for every niche use.
cues.zh: 对其中的每一个我或许都会说好，但很明显，我对全部加起来必须说不。James Gosling 和 Bill Joy 也会这么想。把它们全都加进 Java 编程语言里实在太沉重了。编程词汇中有些部分适合所有程序员使用，但其他部分只适用于各自的特定领域。让所有程序员都背负上掌握或学习每个特定领域所有词汇的负担，这并不公平。

cues.en: We should not make the Java programming language a cathedral, but a plain bizarre might be too loose. What we need is more like a shopping mall, where there are not quite as many choices, but most of the goods are well designed and sellers stand behind what they sell. I could speak at length on the ways in which a shopping mall is like a cathedral, but not here, not now. Now the user could define objects for such numbers to have methods that act in the right ways, but code to use such numbers would look strange and be slow.
cues.zh: 我们不应把 Java 编程语言建成大教堂，但普通的集市可能又太松散了。我们需要的更像是一个购物中心：选择虽然没那么多，但大多数商品都经过精心设计，卖家也会对所售商品负责。关于购物中心在哪些方面像大教堂，我大可以长篇大论，但不是在这里，也不是现在。现在，用户可以为这类数定义对象，让方法按正确的方式工作，但使用这些数的代码看起来会很别扭，而且运行缓慢。

cues.en: Programmers used to adding numbers with plus signs would kvetch. In fact, the Java programming language does have a class of big numbers that have methods for adding them and telling which is larger and all the rest. And you cannot use the plus sign to add such numbers. And programmers who have to use them do kvetch. Generic types and overloaded operators would let a user code up all of these, and in such a way that they would look in all ways just like the types that are built in. They would let users grow the Java programming language.
cues.zh: 习惯用加号做加法的程序员会发牢骚。事实上，Java 语言确实有一类大数，它们有方法做加法、判断哪个更大等等。而你不能用加号来加这种数。不得不用它们的程序员确实会发牢骚。泛型和重载运算符能让用户把这一切都写出来，而且各方面都像内置类型一样。它们能让用户扩展 Java 语言。

cues.en: in a smooth and clean way. And it would not just be for numbers. Generic types would be good for coding hash sets, for example. And there are many other uses. And each user would not have to code up such number classes each for his own use. When a language gives you the right tools, such classes can be coded by a few and then put up as libraries for others to use, or not as they choose. But they don't have to be built in as part of the base language. If you give a person a fish, he can eat for a day. If you teach a person to fish,
cues.zh: 以顺畅而干净的方式。而且这不止适用于数字。比如，泛型也很适合编写哈希集合。还有很多其他用途。每个用户不必各自为自己的用途编写这样的数字类。当语言给了你合适的工具，这类类可以由少数人编写，然后作为库发布给其他人使用，或者由他们自己选择不用。但它们不必作为基础语言的一部分内置。给人一条鱼，他能吃一天。教人钓鱼，

cues.en: He can eat his whole life long. If you give a person tools, he can make a fishing pole and lots of other tools. He can build a machine to crank out fishing poles. In this way, he can help others to catch fish. Meta means that you step back from your own place. What you used to do is now what you see. What you were is now what you act on. Verbs turn to nouns. What you used to think of as a pattern
cues.zh: 他就能吃一辈子。给人工具，他就能做出鱼竿和很多其他工具。他能造出机器来批量生产鱼竿。这样，他就能帮助别人钓鱼。元意味着从自己的位置后退一步。你过去做的事，现在成了你看到的东西。你过去是什么，现在成了你作用的对象。动词变成名词。你过去认为是一种模式的东西

cues.en: is now treated as a thing to put in the slot of an other pattern. A meta-foo is a foo in whose slots you can put parts of a foo. In a way, a language design of the old school is a pattern for programs. But now we need to go meta. We should now think of a language design as being a pattern for language designs, a tool for making more tools of the same kind. This is the nub of what I want to say. A language design can no longer be a thing.
cues.zh: 现在被当作可以放进另一个模式槽位里的东西。元 foo 是一个 foo，你可以把 foo 的各个部分放进它的槽位里。某种程度上，旧派的语言设计是程序的模式。但现在我们需要走向元层面。我们现在应该把语言设计看作语言设计的模式，看作制造更多同类工具的工具。这就是我想说的核心。语言设计不能再是一个东西。

cues.en: It must be a pattern, a pattern for growth, a pattern for growing the pattern, for defining the patterns that programmers can use for their real work and their main goal. My point is that a good programmer in these times does not just write programs. A good programmer builds a working vocabulary. In other words, a good programmer does language design, though not from scratch, but building on the frame of a base language. In the course of giving this talk, because I started with a small language,
cues.zh: 它必须是一种模式，一种用于生长的模式，一种用于生长这个模式的模式，用来定义程序员可用于实际工作和主要目标的模式。我的观点是，如今的好程序员不只是写程序。好程序员会建立一套工作词汇。换句话说，好程序员做语言设计，但不是从头开始，而是在基础语言的框架上构建。在讲这次演讲的过程中，因为我从一门小语言开始，

cues.en: I've had to define 50 or more new words or phrases and 16 names of persons or things. And I laid out six rules for making new words from old ones. In this way, I added to the base language. If I were to write a book, starting from just the words of one syllable, I am sure that I would have to define hundreds of new words. It should give no one pause to note that the writing of a program having a million lines of code might need many, many hundreds of new words. That is to say,
cues.zh: 我不得不定义 50 多个新词或短语，以及 16 个人名或事物名。我还列出了六条从旧词造新词的规则。这样，我就扩展了基础语言。如果我要写一本书，只从单音节词开始，我确信我得定义几百个新词。写一个百万行代码的程序可能需要成百上千个新词，这不应让人迟疑。也就是说，

cues.en: a new language built on the base language. I will be so bold as to say that it cannot be done any other way. Well, there may be one other way, which is to use a large, rich programming language that has grown over tens or hundreds of years, that has all we need to say what we want to say, that we are taught as we grow up and take for granted. It may be that a hundred years from now, there will be a programming language that by then has stood the test of time.
cues.zh: 一门建立在基础语言之上的新语言。我敢大胆地说，不可能用别的方式做到。嗯，也许还有一种办法，就是使用一门庞大而丰富的编程语言，它经过几十年甚至几百年发展，拥有我们表达所需的一切，是我们从小被教导、并习以为常的。也许一百年后，会出现一门到那时已经经受住时间考验的编程语言。

cues.en: needs no more changes for most uses and is used by all persons who write programs because each child learns it in school. But that is not where we are now. So, language design is not at all the same kind of work it was 30 years ago or 20 years ago. Back then you could set out to design a whole language and then build it yourself or with a small team because it was small and because you would then do with it, what you would then do with it was small. Now programs are big messes with many needs.
cues.zh: 对大多数用途来说，它已无需再改；所有写程序的人都在用它，因为每个孩子在学校就学它。但我们现在并不是这样。所以，语言设计这项工作，和30年前、20年前完全不是一回事了。那时候，你可以着手设计一整门语言，然后自己或带一个小团队把它做出来，因为它很小，而且你随后用它做的事也很小。现在程序都是一大团乱麻，有各种各样的需求。

cues.en: A small language won't do the job. If you design a big language all at once, and then try to build it all at once, it will fail. You will end up late, and some other small language will take your place. It would be great if there were some small programming language that felt large. The way basic English is small, but feels large in some ways. But I don't know how to do it, and I have good cause to doubt that it can be done at all. In its day, APL was a small language that felt large. But our needs have grown,
cues.zh: 小语言干不了这活。如果你一次性设计一门大语言，再想一次性把它造出来，那会失败。你会拖到很晚，然后别的某种小语言会取代你。要是能有某种小而感觉很大的编程语言，那就太好了。就像基础英语很小，但在某些方面感觉很大。可我不知道该怎么做，而且我有充分理由怀疑这事到底能不能做到。APL 在它的时代就是一门小而感觉很大的语言。但我们的需求已经增长了，

cues.en: and APL did not have a good pattern for growth. So I think the sole way to win is to plan for growth, to plan for growth with help from users. This is a win for you because you have help. This is a win for the users because they get to have their say and get to bend the growth to their needs. But you need to have one or more persons to, or one or more groups, to take on the task of judging and testing and sifting what the users do and say, and adding what they think best to the big pile of code.
cues.zh: 而 APL 没有一套好的成长模式。所以我认为，唯一取胜之道就是为成长做规划，借助用户的帮助来规划成长。这对你是好事，因为你能得到帮助。这对用户也是好事，因为他们能发表意见，让语言的发展贴合自己的需求。但你得有一个或多个人，或者一个或多个小组，来承担判断、测试和筛选用户所做所说的任务，并把他们认为最好的部分加入那一大堆代码里。

cues.en: in the hope that other users will trust what they say and not have to go to all the work to test and judge and sift each new claim or each new piece of code, each for his own self. Parts of the language must be designed to help the task of growth, of growing the language. A good set of types, ways for a user to define new types, to add new words and new rules to the language, to define and use all sorts of patterns. All these are needed.
cues.zh: 希望其他用户能信任他们的话，不必每个人都亲自费尽力气去测试、判断和筛选每一条新主张或每一段新代码。语言中的某些部分必须设计得有助于成长这项任务，也就是让语言生长。要有一套好的类型，要让用户能定义新类型，能向语言里加入新词和新规则，能定义并使用各种模式。这些都需要。

cues.en: The designer should not, for example, define 20 kinds of number types in the language. But there will be users who, all told, beg for 20 different kinds of numbers. This is hard. The language should have a way for the user to define number types that work well with each other, and with plus signs and other such signs, and with the many ways of pushing bits in and out of the computer.
cues.zh: 比如，设计者不该在语言里定义20种数值类型。但总会有用户合起来要求20种不同的数。这很难。语言应该让用户能定义彼此配合良好的数值类型，也要能配合加号之类的符号，还要能配合把比特送进送出计算机的多种方式。

cues.en: One might define just one or two number types at the start to show how it ought to be done. Then, leave the rest of the users. Help them all as best you can to work side by side and not nose to nose. You may find that you need to add warts as part of the design so that you can get it out the door fast with the goal of taking out the warts at a later time. Now there are warts and then there are warts. With care, one can design a wart
cues.zh: 一开始可以只定义一两种数值类型，示范应该怎么做。然后，剩下的交给用户。尽你所能帮他们并肩工作，而不是鼻子顶鼻子地对着干。你可能会发现，需要把一些瑕疵作为设计的一部分加进去，好让语言快速发布，目标是以后再把这些瑕疵去掉。不过瑕疵也分三六九等。用心的话，可以设计一个瑕疵，

cues.en: so that it will not be too hard to take out or patch up later on. But if you do not take care at the start, you may be stuck for years to come with a wart you did not plan. Some warts are not bad things you put in, but good things you leave out. Have a plan to add those good things later, if you should choose to do so. And make sure that other parts of your design don't cut you off from adding those good things when the time is right. I hope to bring these thoughts to bear on the Java programming language. The Java programming language
cues.zh: 让它以后不会太难去掉或修补。但如果你一开始不用心，可能会在未来好几年里被一个你没计划过的瑕疵困住。有些瑕疵不是你放进去的坏东西，而是你漏掉的好东西。要有个计划，以后如果决定要做，就把那些好东西加进去。还要确保设计的其他部分不会在时机成熟时挡住你加入那些好东西。我希望把这些想法用到 Java 编程语言上。Java 编程语言

cues.en: has done as well as it has up to now because it started small, I think. It was not hard to learn, and it was not hard to port. It has grown quite a bit since then. If the design of the Java programming language, as it is now, had been put forth three years ago, it would have failed. Of that, I am sure. Programmers would have cried, too big, too much hair. I can't deal with all that.
cues.zh: 之所以到现在为止能做得这么好，我想是因为它起步时很小。它不难学，也不难移植。从那以后它已经长大了不少。如果把现在这样的 Java 编程语言设计放到三年前提出，它会失败。这一点我很确定。程序员们会大喊：太大了，太复杂了。我应付不了这些。

cues.en: But in real life, it worked out fine because the users have grown with the language and learned it piece by piece. And they buy into it because they've had some say in how to change the language. And the Java programming language needs to grow yet some more, but I hope not a lot more. At least, I think only a few more rules are needed. And the rest can be done with libraries, most of them built by users and not by Sun. If we add hundreds of new things to the Java brand programming language,
cues.zh: 但在现实中，结果还不错，因为用户随着这门语言一起成长，一点一点学会了它。他们之所以接受它，是因为他们对语言该如何改变有过发言权。Java 编程语言还需要再成长一些，但我希望别成长太多。至少我认为只需要再加几条规则。其余的事可以交给库来做，其中大多数库由用户而不是 Sun 构建。如果我们往 Java 品牌的编程语言里加入数百个新东西，

cues.en: We will have a huge language, but it will take a long time to get there. But if we add a few things, just the right things, generic types, operator overloading, user-defined types of lightweight for use as numbers and small vectors and such, and some other things that are designed to let users make and add things for their own use, I think we can go a long way and much faster. We need to put tools for language growth in the hands of users.
cues.zh: 我们就会得到一门庞大的语言，但要花很长时间才能走到那一步。可如果我们只加少量东西——恰到好处的东西：泛型、运算符重载、可用作数值和小向量之类的用户定义轻量级类型，以及其他让用户能为自己制作和添加东西的设计——我觉得我们能走很远，而且快得多。我们需要把语言成长的工具交到用户手里。

cues.en: I hope that we can, in this way or some other way, design a programming language where we don't seem to spend most of our time talking and writing in words of just one syllable. One of the good things I can say for short words is that they make for short talks. They gave me an hour and a half for this talk, and I have used less than an hour. Once I am done, you will have time to go out in the hall, have a cup of tea, and talk with your friends. But first, I would like to tell you what I have learned from the task of designing this talk.
cues.zh: 我希望我们能以这种方式或其他方式，设计出一种编程语言，让我们看起来不会把大部分时间都花在用单音节词说话和写作上。短词的一个好处是，它们让演讲也短。他们给了我一个半小时做这场演讲，而我用了不到一小时。等我讲完，你们就有时间走到大厅里，喝杯茶，和朋友聊聊。但首先，我想告诉各位，我从设计这场演讲这项任务中学到了什么。

cues.en: In choosing to give up the many long words that I have come to know since I was a child, words that have many fine shades of meaning, I made this task much harder than it needs to be. I hope that you have not found it too hard on your ears. But I found that sticking to this rule made me think. I had to take time to think through how to phrase each thought. And there was this choice for each new word. Is it worth the work to define it?
cues.zh: 选择放弃我从小熟知的大量长词——那些有着丰富细微含义的词——让这项任务变得比实际需要的难得多。我希望各位没有觉得听起来太费劲。但我发现，坚守这条规则逼着我思考。我得花时间想清楚每个想法该怎么措辞。而且每遇到一个新词，都要做选择：值得费劲去定义它吗？

cues.en: Or should I just stick with the words I have? Should I do the work of defining a new word such as mirror? Or should I just say looking glass each time I want to speak of one? As an example, I was tempted more than once to state the L-Y rule for making new words that change what verbs mean. But in the end, I chose to cast all such words to one side and make do. And I came that close to defining the word without. But each time, for better or for worse, I found some other way to phrase my thought.
cues.zh: 还是我该就用手头已有的词？我该费劲去定义像 mirror 这样的新词吗？还是每次想说到它时，就干脆说 looking glass？举个例子，我不止一次想宣布 L-Y 规则，用它来造改变动词含义的新词。但最后，我选择把这类词统统搁到一边，凑合应付。我还就差那么一点，就要去定义 without 这个词了。但每一次，不管好坏，我都找到了别的说法来表达想法。

cues.en: I learned in my youth, from the books of such great teachers of writing as Strunk and White, that it is better to choose short words than I can. I should not choose long, hard words just to make other persons think that I know a lot. I should try to make my thoughts clear. If they are clear and right, then other persons can judge my work as it ought to be judged. And I am sure you will. From the work of planning this talk, in which I have tried to go with this rule of short words,
cues.zh: 我年轻时从 Strunk and White 等写作名家的书里学到，能选短词时就选短词。我不该为了让人以为我懂得多，就挑又长又难的词。我该努力把想法讲清楚。如果想法清楚又正确，别人就能恰如其分地评判我的工作。我相信各位会这样做的。在筹划这场演讲的过程中，我一直努力遵守这条短词规则，

cues.en: much farther than in the past, I found that for the most part, they were right. Short words work well, if we choose them well. Thus, I think that programming languages need to be more like the languages that we speak. But it might be good too if we were to use the languages we speak more in the way that we now use programming languages. All in all, I think it might be a good thing if those who rule our lives, those in high places who do the work of state, those who judge what we do,
cues.zh: 而且走得比过去远得多，我发现，大多数时候他们是对的。短词确实好用，前提是我们选得好。因此，我认为编程语言需要更像我们说的语言。但同样可能不错的是，我们也能更多按如今使用编程语言的方式来使用我们说的语言。总而言之，我认为如果那些支配我们生活的人、那些身居高位从事国务的人、那些评判我们所作所为的人，

cues.en: And most of all those who make the laws were made to define their terms and say all else that they say in words of one syllable. For I have found that this mode of speech makes it hard to hedge. It takes work and great care and some skill to find just the right way to say what you want to say. But in the end, you seem to have no choice but to talk straight. If you do not veer wide of the truth, you are forced to hit it dead on. I urge you, too, to give it a try. Thank you.
cues.zh: 尤其是那些制定法律的人，都被要求定义自己的术语，并且用单音节词来说他们要说的一切，那可能是件好事。因为我发现，这种说话方式很难含糊其辞。要找到恰好的方式说出你想说的话，需要费功夫、极其小心，还得有点技巧。但到最后，你似乎别无选择，只能直说。只要不偏离真相太远，你就被迫一针见血。我也敦促各位试一试。谢谢。
